Name: Y Combinator
Stage: Idea-stage: yes (no product, no revenue, no incorporation needed to apply; YC FAQ: about 40% of funded companies are 'just an idea'). Solo founders accepted.
Check size terms: $500,000 total: $125,000 post-money SAFE for 7% + $375,000 uncapped MFN SAFE; pro rata rights; no fees
Sectors: Sector-agnostic (heavy AI/software weighting in recent batches)
Geography: Global applicants; program is in-person in San Francisco (3-day kickoff + weekly SF meetups). No remote/online batch option is offered as of 2026-09-02.
Application timing: batch; Winter 2027 on-time deadline 2026-11-02 8pm PT (decision by 2026-12-11); Early Decision open for Spring/Summer/Fall batches; four batches per year
Best channel: application form
Notes: Accepts idea-stage and unincorporated teams; ~40% of each batch is idea-only. Batch is in-person in SF; the remote-batch era (2020-2021) is over. Late applications are still reviewed but on-time gives a decision by a fixed date.

Name: Antler
Stage: Idea-stage: yes (pre-team, pre-idea accepted; residency is designed to match co-founders and build from 'Day Zero'). Antler Elevate handles Series A+ separately.
Check size terms: Varies by location. Antler Disrupt Deal (2026-01-05): $400K = $250K for 10% via SAFE + $150K uncapped MFN SAFE. Singapore/Japan 2026: $150K for 10% ($100K for 10% + $50K uncapped MFN SAFE) + up to $250K matching. Antler India AI Residency: INR 4Cr (~$470K) for 11% + up to $30M follow-on.
Sectors: Sector-agnostic; 2026 emphasis on AI
Geography: Global: 26 locations across APAC (incl. India/Bangalore), Europe, Americas, Middle East/Africa. Residencies are in-person per city.
Application timing: rolling by location; residencies/sprints run throughout the year. Antler India: 'Next Residency will be announced soon' (no date on 2026-09-02).
Best channel: application form
Notes: Backs individuals before a company exists and helps form teams during the residency. Deal terms differ by country; check the local residency page. Antler India (X: @AntlerIndia) runs a Bangalore AI Residency: 3-week decision, INR 4Cr for 11%, INR 2L relocation grant, in-person first 2 weeks.

Name: Entrepreneur First (EF)
Stage: Idea-stage: yes (pre-team, pre-idea, pre-company; individuals are assessed 'before they have a business, cofounder or an idea').
Check size terms: Equity-free grant during ideation; up to $250K investment once a company is formed (equity % not stated on site); up to $5M follow-on through future rounds; $600K+ credits; 9 months office space
Sectors: Sector-agnostic; deep tech and AI focus
Geography: London, Bangalore, San Francisco (in-person). Visa help possible for other locations.
Application timing: batch; Bangalore programme early deadline 2026-10-05 (start Feb 2027); London programme start Apr 2027; SF 'Bridge Residency' start Feb 2027; XF2 London start Fall 2026
Best channel: application form
Notes: Talent investor: no cofounder or idea needed to apply. Pays a grant while you find a cofounder and idea, then invests when you incorporate. Contact via form at joinef.com/contact/ only.

Name: Pioneer (pioneer.app)
Stage: Idea-stage: yes historically (online tournament for side projects and early ideas), but the program is CLOSED: 'We stopped making new investments in 2024'.
Check size terms: unknown (program closed to new investments since 2024)
Sectors: Sector-agnostic (historical)
Geography: Global, fully online (historical: 300+ founders in 50+ countries)
Application timing: closed; no new investments since 2024
Best channel: application form
Notes: Founded 2018 by Daniel Gross and Rishi Narang; backed by Stripe and Marc Andreessen. Official site states it stopped making new investments in 2024. Do not spend outreach effort here; listed for completeness.

Name: Z Fellows
Stage: Idea-stage: yes (side projects, no company needed: 'No. We can help you set up one.'; 'no such thing as too early').
Check size terms: $10,000 investment at a $1B valuation cap (converts at next priced round); participation without investment also possible
Sectors: Technical builders, sector-agnostic
Geography: Global ('You can be based anywhere'); mostly virtual, last day in-person in SF or NYC
Application timing: rolling; no deadline; multiple 1-week cohorts per year
Best channel: application form
Notes: 1-week program with ten builders and founders of $1B+ companies. Founder Cory Levy reviews applications personally and posts about it on X. Prior rejections may reapply.

Name: Neo (Neo Residency, formerly Neo Accelerator)
Stage: Idea-stage: yes (targets very early startups and 'high-agency student teams'; students get grants before a company exists).
Check size terms: Neo Residency (announced Feb 2026): $750K uncapped SAFE + $450K+ compute credits; Neo gets participation rights up to 5% in next equity round. Student teams: $40K grant per person + $100K+ credits. Profit share in Neo fund for every founder/student.
Sectors: Sector-agnostic; strong AI focus (Microsoft and OpenAI mentorship for AI companies)
Geography: US-based program: 3 months SF workspace + 2-week Oregon bootcamp; global applicants
Application timing: rolling ('applications are open... rolling basis'); no fixed deadline found on 2026-09-02
Best channel: application form
Notes: Neo Residency replaced Neo Accelerator in Feb 2026; small cohorts (12-15 startups, 5-8 student teams). Neo was Cursor's first investor. Neo.com is JS-rendered; terms above come from Neo's official Substack.

Name: South Park Commons (SPC Founder Fellowship)
Stage: Idea-stage: yes (no finalized idea required: 'No, but you do need to show us how you generate ideas').
Check size terms: $400K upfront for 7% on a standard SAFE + $600K guaranteed in next external round ($1M total); up to $1M in credits
Sectors: Sector-agnostic; technical and research-heavy founders
Geography: San Francisco, New York City, Bangalore (8-week in-person bootcamp, then residency)
Application timing: batch; two cohorts per year. Fall 2026 deadline was 2026-08-02 (closed). Spring 2026 deadline was 2026-02-01; Spring 2027 deadline not yet announced on 2026-09-02.
Best channel: application form
Notes: Fellowship for founders in the '-1 to 0' phase; 8-week bootcamp then open-ended residency. Official site footer links x.com/spc; older posts appear under @southpkcommons. Member Residency is a separate track for technologists who may not want to start a company yet.

Name: Techstars
Stage: Idea-stage: partial. Pre-revenue accepted but evidence of progress expected; many admitted teams already raised $1M-$5M. The Founder Catalyst pre-accelerator targets idea-stage founders.
Check size terms: $220,000: $200,000 uncapped MFN SAFE + $20,000 CEA for 5% common stock (APAC programs: $100,000 MFN SAFE + $20K CEA)
Sectors: Sector-agnostic; many vertical programs (healthcare, AI health, workforce, etc.)
Geography: Global: Boston, Boulder, Chicago, London, NYC, Tokyo, Los Angeles and others; 'Techstars Anywhere' is remote-first
Application timing: batch; Spring 2027 applications opened 2026-08-24, NYC final deadline 2026-11-18 (program starts 2027-03-08). Deadlines vary by program.
Best channel: application form
Notes: 3-month mentorship-driven program; terms mirror YC structure since April 2025. Best fit for teams with some traction; pure idea-stage founders should look at Techstars Founder Catalyst. Only address found on site is privacy@techstars.com (not for applications).

Name: Pear VC (PearX)
Stage: Idea-stage: yes ('Any founder starting a company is eligible'; most teams have not raised before; solo founders accepted).
Check size terms: $500K to $2M per company, terms negotiated per company ('we'll work with you')
Sectors: Sector-agnostic; AI, enterprise, biotech, consumer verticals with partner expertise
Geography: In-person in San Francisco Bay Area (Pear Studio SF and Menlo Park); 12-week program; global applicants must relocate
Application timing: batch; PearX W27 regular deadline 2026-10-04; two cohorts per year (Winter Jan-Apr, Summer Jul-Oct); funds year-round
Best channel: application form
Notes: Small cohorts (~20-25 teams); all partners are former founders or operators. Starts working with teams before the cohort begins. Contact only via form at pear.vc/contact-us.

Name: HF0
Stage: Idea-stage: yes, but only for REPEAT founders ('The residency for repeat founders'). First-time founders are not the target.
Check size terms: unknown on official site; secondary sources (2025-2026) report $1M uncapped SAFE for 5%
Sectors: Sector-agnostic; heavy AI representation
Geography: San Francisco, live-in 12-week residency (secondary sources); 10 teams per batch
Application timing: batch; site lists 'Batch Starts: September 13' and 'Batch Starts: January 4' with Demo Days 'December 4' / 'Dec 1'; no application deadline posted on 2026-09-02
Best channel: application form / Twitter DM
Notes: 'Startup monastery' model: housing, meals, no distractions, 10 teams at a time. Dave Fontenot invites repeat unicorn founders to DM him on X. Official site publishes batch dates and outcome facts but not deal terms.

Name: Founders, Inc. (f.inc)
Stage: Idea-stage: yes (first check; solo founders accepted; pre-revenue frontier-tech teams; Blueprint II expects a team building hardware/frontier tech, no revenue needed)
Check size terms: Blueprint II: $150k per team upfront for 5% on a SAFE, no MFN, plus $1M+ in credits. General first checks: $100k-$250k.
Sectors: Hardware and frontier tech: robotics, drones, space, advanced manufacturing, energy, new materials, biosciences, frontier AI models, chips, AR/VR, content creation
Geography: San Francisco (Fort Mason campus), in-person; international founders accepted if they can be in SF and secure their own US entry permission
Application timing: batch (Blueprint II): deadline September 14, 2026 11:59 PM PST; program Sept 30 - Dec 11, 2026; applications reviewed on a rolling basis, reply by Sept 20
Best channel: application form; lab@f.inc is published on the site, so cold email is possible
Notes: 3-month in-person program at a 42,000 sq ft campus with hardware labs, then up to 1 year of lab residence. They call themselves 'often the first believers'. Founders pay their own travel and housing. Founder/GP: Furqan Rydhan (thirdweb co-founder).

Name: a16z Speedrun
Stage: Idea-stage: yes (solo founders accepted; they aim to be the first check; also accept early companies that already raised). Must be full-time and able to build the product in-house.
Check size terms: Up to $1M: $500K for 10% upfront on a SAFE, plus $500K in the next round within 18 months; $10M+ in cloud/AI/software credits; pro rata rights; no board seat
Sectors: Sector-agnostic (team roots in games, AI, consumer tech)
Geography: Founders from around the world; in-person attendance in San Francisco required
Application timing: rolling year-round; priority window October 12 - November 1, 2026 for cohort SR008 (late January - April 2027, San Francisco); two cohorts per year
Best channel: application form; sr-team@a16z.com is published for questions
Notes: 12-week program that ends in a Demo Day. Acceptance rate stated as lower than 0.4%. Funds are wired at close; a16z says it doubles down in future rounds. Jon Lai (@Tocelot) is the GP on the speedrun team.

Name: Sequoia Arc
Stage: Idea-stage: partial. Open call is for pre-seed and seed stage founders. Sequoia cites backing 'Nvidia with just the founding team' and 'Wiz when there wasn't a clear idea', but a founding team/company is expected.
Check size terms: unknown (official: 'any terms are company specific'); third-party sites report about $1M upfront, not verified on the official site
Sectors: Sector-agnostic
Geography: Not restricted on the official page; third-party sources report San Francisco and London cohorts (unverified)
Application url: https://www.sequoiacap.com/arc/ (apply link appears only while the open call is active; no apply link visible on 2026-09-02)
Application timing: batch, bi-annual open call; last verified close date: Sunday August 17, 2025 11:59 pm PT (Sequoia X post); no 2026 deadline visible on the official page on 2026-09-02
Best channel: application form during the open call; Sequoia also says it finds founders via cold outreach
Notes: Arc Intensive: 4 days, about 10 companies per cohort, workshops with Sequoia partners (Jess Lee, Alfred Lin, Roelof Botha named). Benefits package includes 200+ perks (NVIDIA up to $500k savings, Azure up to $350k credits).

Name: a16z START
Stage: Idea-stage: yes at launch in 2022 ('even if you don't yet have a fully formed idea and haven't yet quit your day job'). Current state: no live program page found.
Check size terms: 2022 terms: up to $1M from the a16z seed fund, equity undisclosed. Current terms: unknown.
Sectors: 2022 categories: American dynamism, consumer, enterprise, fintech, games, other
Geography: Remote-first at launch (2022)
Application url: unknown (former URL https://a16z.com/programs-a16z-start/ now 301-redirects to /seed/, which lands on the a16z portfolio page filtered to Seed)
Application timing: unknown (was rolling in 2022)
Best channel: none found; a16z's current early-stage program is Speedrun (apply there)
Notes: CURRENT STATE (verified 2026-09-02): a16z START appears inactive. The 2022 announcement post is still online, but a16z.com/start is a 404 and the old program URL redirects to the seed portfolio page. The a16z site navigation lists Speedrun as its program. No official closure or merger notice was found; treat 'merged into Speedrun' as an inference, not a verified fact.

Name: Afore Capital
Stage: Idea-stage: yes. Main fund invests in 'pre-traction, pre-everything companies'. Founders-in-Residence (FIR) accepts people with 'nothing more than the will to start a company with a Google doc of ideas', solo or teams.
Check size terms: Main fund: $500k - $2M+ pre-seed ($500M fund). FIR: at least $100K guaranteed, customized terms, typical range $250k-750k. FIR University (students/recent grads): $20-100k on a YC-style SAFE.
Sectors: Generalist (not specified on site)
Geography: FIR is in-person for 2 months in South Park, San Francisco; fund geography not specified
Application timing: rolling year-round; FIR kickoff dates: Fall 2026 (Oct 1), Spring 2027 (Feb 1); FIR University accepts teams monthly on a rolling basis
Best channel: application form (Airtable/Typeform); no public email found
Notes: FIR wants technical builders with 2+ years work experience who are ready to go full-time. Afore says it can 'sign docs & wire next-day'. Partners: Gaurav Jain (@gjain) and Anamitra Banerji (@anamitra). Fund 4 is $185M (TechCrunch, Feb 2025).

Name: Precursor Ventures
Stage: Idea-stage: yes. 'We do not have requirements for traction or metrics'; they want the first institutional round and back unproven first-time founders. A company or founding plan is expected.
Check size terms: Typically up to $500,000 in pre-seed and seed rounds; they leave room for syndication; instrument not stated
Sectors: Generalist software and hardware (portfolio: fintech, healthcare, SaaS, consumer)
Geography: Companies headquartered in North America (USA, Canada, Mexico); other geographies considered
Application timing: rolling; 30-40 new investments per year; reply can take at least 2-4 weeks
Best channel: application form; hello@precursorvc.com is published for general inquiries, so cold email is possible
Notes: 'We invest in people over product.' Solo-GP style firm led by Charles Hudson, about $250M AUM. Committed to founder diversity. Runs a London bootcamp for UK/EU founders raising US pre-seed (May 2026).

Name: 1517 Fund
Stage: Idea-stage: yes. $50,000 checks at the idea/R&D stage; Medici Project gives $1k grants for projects with no company; backs dropouts, students, and scientists 'long before they know they'll become founders'.
Check size terms: Fund: $50,000 (idea/R&D stage) to $1,000,000 (deep tech/sci-fi seed); average $400,000 pre-seed check. Medici Project: minimum $1k no-strings cash grant, no equity, no IP claim.
Sectors: Software, hardware with data plays, deep tech/sci-fi tech, biotech; 'more about the who than the what'
Geography: Global community; Medici grants limited to North America
Application url: https://www.1517fund.com/ (embedded form); Medici: https://www.1517fund.com/medici (email a 5-minute Loom video)
Application timing: rolling; in-thesis applicants hear back within about two weeks, sometimes within a few days
Best channel: application form or cold email ('Write in! We read all submissions'; team reachable at firstname@1517fund.com)
Notes: Backs dropouts, renegade students, and deep tech scientists; no degree needed. GPs Danielle Strachman and Michael Gibson ran the Thiel Fellowship. Medici grants are paid by Venmo with no strings attached.

Name: Hustle Fund
Stage: Idea-stage: partial. Pre-seed only ('Not seed'); the stated sweet spot is a team with at least an MVP; they want 'an ambitious idea, evidence of hustle', not metrics. Pre-revenue is fine; pure idea with no product is below their sweet spot.
Check size terms: $150K first check; instrument and valuation not stated on the site
Sectors: Software generalist, SaaS-heavy; excludes pharma, medical devices, art/film, land, restaurants, brick-and-mortar retail
Geography: Mostly United States, Canada, and Southeast Asia
Application timing: rolling, always investing, up to 100 investments per year; decision in 1-2 meetings; reply 24-48 hours after a call; wire in under 1 week
Best channel: application form ('We read everything'); no public email found
Notes: 'Hilariously early' pre-seed software investor. GPs: Elizabeth Yin (@dunkhippo33), Eric Bahn (@ericbahn), Shiyan Koh (@shiyankoh). Runs Angel Squad (2,000+ angels) and Camp Hustle events.

Name: Village Global
Stage: Idea-stage: partial. Invests 'at Day 0' in pre-seed and seed; the $500K-$3M check size implies a formed team and company.
Check size terms: $500K - $3M checks; instrument not stated
Sectors: Generalist ('proud generalists')
Geography: Global
Application url: none; email your deck or memo to hello@villageglobal.com (https://www.villageglobal.com/contact-us)
Application timing: rolling (no deadlines published)
Email: hello@villageglobal.com (visible page text; the mailto link on the same page uses hello@villageglobal.vc)
Best channel: cold email ('Building? Send your deck or memo to hello@villageglobal.com')
Notes: Network-driven firm; LPs include Reid Hoffman (Chairman), Bill Gates, Jeff Bezos, Mark Zuckerberg. GPs: Ben Casnocha (@bencasnocha), Anne Dwane (@adwane), Amrit Rao. Founder Erik Torenberg is Partner Emeritus. Third-party sources cite older $100K-$500K checks; the official site now says $500K-$3M.

Name: Emergent Ventures (Mercatus Center, Tyler Cowen)
Stage: Idea-stage: yes (individuals age 13+; no company needed; 'zero to one' ideas; applications come from students, writers, researchers, founders)
Check size terms: Grant, no equity. Amount not stated on the official page. Third-party sources report a median of about $10k-$25k and a range from a few hundred dollars to $50k+ (unverified).
Sectors: Any field; 'highly scalable, zero to one ideas for meaningfully improving society'; dedicated tracks for India, Africa, the Caribbean, and Ukraine
Geography: Global
Application timing: rolling; no deadline
Best channel: application form (short proposal, about 1,500 words, with bio and ballpark budget); Tyler Cowen reads every proposal
Notes: Low-overhead fellowship and grant program launched in 2018 and administered by Tyler Cowen. Cowen rejects proposals that are 'ambitious and interesting, but lack sufficient detail to convince me that they are feasible' and avoids crowded areas. Decisions are fast and personal. The email was decoded from the Cloudflare-protected mailto link on the official page.

Name: Thiel Fellowship
Stage: Idea-stage: yes (pre-team, pre-company accepted). FAQ: 'You don't need to have incorporated a company or built a full product yet' and 'we review and accept applicants as individuals'. Must be aged 22 or younger and without a university degree; fellows skip or stop out of college.
Check size terms: $250,000 grant spread over two years; no equity ('We do not take equity in your company').
Sectors: Sector-agnostic (science, technology, companies, projects).
Geography: Global (no geographic restriction stated in the FAQ); age 22 or younger.
Application timing: rolling ('we accept applications year round'). No deadline.
Best channel: application form (rolling). A general team email exists, but the site directs applicants to the form.
Notes: Looks for young people who 'want to build new things' and 'take on big risks' instead of following a traditional track. Applicants are judged as individuals, so no cofounder or company is needed. Grant was raised to $250K from the class of 2026 (third-party reports).

Name: 776 Foundation Fellowship (776 Fellowship)
Stage: Idea-stage: yes (projects, not companies; pre-company accepted). Official text: two-year, full-time program for 18-24 year olds 'to work on projects to fight climate change instead of pursuing a university degree'.
Check size terms: $100,000 grant over two years, paid quarterly; no equity (grant).
Sectors: Climate change (2025 review page also mentions 'Climate and Frontier Innovation').
Geography: Global ('Fellows must be ages 18 to 24 and can live anywhere in the world'; final remote interview).
Application url: https://www.776.org/ (application form appears on the site when a cycle is open; email signup for notification otherwise)
Application timing: batch. Program still runs. Site text (from the site JS bundle): 'Check back later this year for our 2026 Application' and 'Our 5th Cohort will be selected May 2026, with a start date of June 2026'. Past windows opened late March and closed mid April (2025 deadline: April 14). Current open/closed status for the 2026 window: unknown (site is JS-rendered; text may be stale).
Best channel: application form (when the cycle is open); sign up on the site for the opening notice. No cold-email address published.
Notes: Inspired by the Thiel Fellowship; ~20 fellows per cohort; fellows leave or skip university to work full time on a climate project. Funded by Alexis Ohanian's 776 Foundation ($20M commitment). Site lists a '2025 776 Fellowship Year in Review', so the program was active in 2025.

Name: Soma Capital (Soma Fellows / direct)
Stage: Idea-stage: yes for Soma Fellows (official site: 'check out our fellows program if you're just getting started'; third-party listings: open to anyone building early-stage companies, skews to founders in early-to-mid 20s and students). Direct fund invests pre-seed/seed.
Check size terms: Official fellows page: 'Track 1: Up to $2m uncapped for your startup' with 'potential fast 10m+ follow on funding for strong traction'. Instrument and equity not stated on the official page. Third-party listings report a typical $100K uncapped SAFE.
Sectors: Generalist; AI/ML and data infrastructure prominent in portfolio (OpenAI, Anthropic, Databricks listed).
Geography: Global; office space in SF and NY (third-party: also Boston; remote participation with optional in-person events).
Application timing: unknown. Third-party listings conflict: one lists Spring and Fall cohorts (Spring 2026 deadline April 1, 2026; Fall programming Oct 10 to Nov 17), another calls it 'a rolling fellowship'. The official page shows no deadline.
Best channel: application form; cold outreach accepted (Soma's X post invites past applicants to 'shoot us a note with updates').
Notes: Looks for 'brilliant superhumans pushing humanity forward'; claims 40+ unicorns seeded. Track 2 of the fellows program places engineers into portfolio companies. Weekly dinners and events with unicorn founders are part of the program (third-party).

Name: LAUNCH / Founder University (Jason Calacanis)
Stage: Idea-stage: yes ('12-week pre-accelerator for 0-to-1'; built for founders in 'Year Zero' and Year One; idea, MVP, or existing product all accepted).
Check size terms: Official: '$25K or $125K' invested into top graduates; instrument and equity not stated on the site. Third-party: $125K for 7% on a post-money SAFE, optional follow-on up to $375K on an uncapped MFN SAFE. Tuition $500, refundable if you join every live session.
Sectors: Tech startups, generalist (B2B and B2C).
Geography: Virtual (global) with optional in-person components; LAUNCH is based in the US.
Application timing: rolling ('You can apply to Founder University at any time... Upon acceptance, founders will be assigned to the next cohort'). Site text lists 'Cohort 13 — Early 2026'; a third-party list says Cohort 13 is Fall 2026. Exact next cohort start: unknown.
Best channel: application form; cold email possible (founderu@launch.co is in the official site code).
Notes: 'We invest in founders who show up, ship fast, and never stop building.' Two live virtual sessions per week; investment goes only to top graduates. LAUNCH Accelerator ($125K, 14 weeks) is the later-stage sibling program.

Name: On Deck Founders (ODF)
Stage: Idea-stage: yes (pre-company, pre-team). Admissions page: ideal candidates are '100% committed (or soon committing) to starting a company'; not suitable if you 'already raised beyond pre-seed' or 'already have a team'.
Check size terms: No investment. Non-dilutive ('We don't take any equity'). Pay-what-you-can fee, suggested $1000 USD. $800k+ in perks (AWS, Stripe, Mercury, Carta).
Sectors: Generalist; cohort is >50% technical.
Geography: Global applicants; one-week in-person program in San Francisco; then online community.
Application timing: batch. joinodf.com says next cohort ODF28 launches Q1 2027; admissions.joinodf.com says 'ODF28 kicks off in Q3 2026' (conflict; the main site is likely newer). No deadline published. Process: apply, optional video, interview, decision in ~36 hours.
Best channel: application form. Admissions page also lists founders@joinodf.com.
Notes: beondeck.com now redirects to joinodf.com; ODF is a one-week SF program plus a 3,000+ member community, not an investor. Screens for 'exceptional builder talent and unfair advantages' and 'trajectory over resume'. Claims 1,000+ startups launched and $2B+ raised by alumni.

Name: Conviction Embed (Sarah Guo)
Stage: Idea-stage: yes (pre-company, solo founders accepted). Official FAQ: 'I just got started/haven't incorporated/don't have a cofounder. Am I too early to apply? No!'
Check size terms: $250K on an uncapped, no-discount MFN SAFE (or at the price of a round closed within the last 60 days). Plus $350K AWS credits, $350K Azure credits, and $500K+ other compute/inference/hosting credits.
Sectors: AI-native startups.
Geography: Global applicants; mandatory in-person retreat in San Francisco.
Application timing: batch (about twice a year). Program still runs. Official page: 'Apply early to the 7th cohort', 'Applications are now open', 'Rolling admissions over the month'; retreat September 11-13 and demo day November 12 (no year shown). A third-party listing gives an August 10, 2026 deadline for this cohort, which has passed. Status for cohort 7: likely closed; next cohort date unknown.
Best channel: application form; program email published (embed@conviction.com).
Notes: Eight-week program for AI-native founding teams; some cohort members have already raised. Focus is community, fundraising and hiring workshops, and compute. Founded by Sarah Guo (partner Mike Vernal).

Name: AI Grant (Nat Friedman / Daniel Gross)
Stage: Idea-stage: partly. Targets 'pre-seed/seed-stage startups'; 'no credentials required'; single founders accepted; must be or become a Delaware corporation. 'Demos are a big plus', so a working prototype helps.
Check size terms: $250,000 on an uncapped SAFE ('no cap, no discount MFN SAFE') plus $350,000 in Azure credits and $250,000 in additional credits.
Sectors: AI-native product startups.
Geography: Global; Delaware corporation required.
Application url: unknown (no open form; 'Applications for Batch 4 are closed')
Application timing: batch. Batch 4 closed (applications were due August 9, 2024). No Batch 5 announced as of 2026-09-02; status unknown.
Best channel: application form when a batch opens; follow @aigrant for the announcement. No cold-pitch route published.
Notes: Looks for 'technical & pragmatic founders who want to build great products' and 'smart and energetic people with actionable ideas that are clearly useful'. Backed Perplexity and others. Note: aigrant.org is the older open-source grant; aigrant.com is the equity program.

Name: Betaworks Camp
Stage: Idea-stage: possible but a demo is encouraged. FAQ: a product is 'not required, but having something to show like a demo or beta or Figma is highly encouraged'. Early-stage companies, typically 8-12 per cohort.
Check size terms: Up to $500K per team: 'Betaworks and our syndicate partners will each invest up to $250k'. Spring 2026 terms post: Betaworks Ventures up to $250K on an uncapped SAFE with a 25% discount plus a 5% common stock stake; syndicate up to $250K on uncapped SAFEs with the same discount. No program fee.
Sectors: AI; theme changes per camp (current: 'AI Camp: The New Agent Economy'; Spring 2026: Agent Systems).
Geography: Global applicants; in person in New York (Meatpacking District) for the first and final two weeks; 12-week program.
Application timing: batch. Site banner: 'Application now open for AI Camp: The New Agent Economy' with 'Deadline Extended'; no date published. Fall sessions run August to November; spring sessions March to May (applications Dec-Jan).
Email: unknown (site lists only eventsny@betaworks.com for event inquiries)
Best channel: application form. No program email or cold-pitch route published.
Notes: Thematic camps; the Spring 2026 camp wanted companies 'newly designed assuming agentic AI as a core tenet' and complete, autonomous solutions. Founders pay their own travel and housing in NYC.

Name: 500 Global (Flagship Accelerator)
Stage: Idea-stage: no. Official portal: 'early-stage tech startups'; third-party guides say seed-stage with some traction. A company must exist to take the investment.
Check size terms: $150,000 investment for a 6% stake, 'subject to terms and diligence' (official). Third-party: $37,500 program fee deducted from the investment.
Sectors: Generalist tech.
Geography: Global founders; four-month in-person program in Silicon Valley (Palo Alto / San Francisco).
Application timing: rolling applications ('apply any time of year'). Portal shows Batch 37 open (third-party: Batch 37 starts Q2 2026). The 500.co page still shows stale Batch 36 text (deadline October 11). Current batch number and next deadline: unknown.

Notes: Program gives capital, an expert network and a cohort of web3 teams; curriculum covers PMF, tokenization, GTM, fundraising and regulation. 100+ portfolio companies, for example Phantom and Pimlico.

Name: Boost VC

Geography: unknown (firm based in San Mateo, CA)
Application timing: rolling (about one investment per week; next steps within a week after the first call)

Notes: Stated bar: 'your company must make 1 Billion lives better'. Looks for social, technical or regulatory pressure that forces change. 70+ investments per year; exits include Coinbase.
